method: Recorded at run time, not reconstructed. The campaign was launched, monitored, and closed by the session that authored its profiles; commits, staging, run window, and recovery actions were logged as they happened (campaign-driver.log on each host, EXPERIMENTS.md, and the paper archive's PROVENANCE.txt). Everything below restates those records; nothing is inferred from mtimes.

profile_commit.subject: feat: add 15 validated ideals, promote SYNTCOMP arbiters into ablation corpus

profile_commit_evidence: The launch staging rsynced scripts/ and examples/ to both hosts at this commit (branch feat/ablation-campaign, merged as PR #38 / 3f1cc155), 3.7 hours before the drivers started. It is the commit that fixed the campaign's corpus (TLSF_ABLATION_SPECS at 20 families, H2H_TLSF_SPECS frozen at 12) and the ideals set every row was scored against.
binary_commit_note: Recorded, not inferred: both hosts' checkouts and build-release binaries were at db30a59 at launch, and `git diff db30a59..d02892e -- src include test cmake` is empty, so the staged branch implied no rebuild. The TLSF crash fix a0c0858 was committed mid-campaign (2026-07-25 08:07) and deliberately NOT deployed, so the binary was unchanged for the whole run. This campaign predates the --version commit stamping (PR #45); its CSVs have no commit/dirty columns.

run_window.note: UTC timestamps from each host's campaign-driver.log (drivers launched simultaneously). av3's clock runs ~17 min fast, so its timestamps carry that skew. Post-processing (recompare --all against the frozen ideals, AuRUS ltlsynt validation) continued to 2026-07-27T02:20:38Z on av2. Merged locally 2026-07-27 with the vendored merge_experiments.py.

caveats: AuRUS out-root incident: the AuRUS phase initially ran a harness (f45ad18d) whose relative --out-root resolved against the AuRUS repo, so the first-pass CSVs read 0 solutions. No JVM output was lost; after fix 0f39abe absolutised the flag, a recovery pass backfilled complete runs from the misplaced outputs and re-ran ~60 SIGKILLed runs per host. The aurus_results CSVs here are the product of that fixed pass.

One crash class during the run: the score_population >15%-scoring-failure throw escaped uncaught on the TLSF path (~1/320 runs, load-transient). Affected rows were re-run; the merged CSVs have zero missing rows. The fix (a0c0858) landed on the branch mid-campaign but was not deployed until after close.

AuRUS is not seedable (Settings.RANDOM_GENERATOR from Math.random()); mitigation was 30 repeats per spec with per-run out.txt and Settings archived on the hosts. Its GATO was 3600 s against counter's 600 s wall cap - an asymmetry that favours the baseline.

amba is calibration-only (16 rows, every run capped at 600 s, 0 repairs) and arbiter-aurus is the head-to-head control cell (20 rows); both are excluded from the 3,040-row factorial. The analyse.ipynb exclusion cell enforces this.

vendored_scripts.note: Verbatim copies of the campaign's driver scripts so the directory reproduces without the git history. Each file records the commit it came from and its git blob sha; verify with `git hash-object <file>`. Unlike the retrofitted campaigns, every basis here is a record: the staging of these exact blobs to both hosts was logged at launch (or, for the AuRUS pair, verified against the hosts' still-matching on-disk copies on 2026-07-31). All source commits are ancestors of main via merge 3f1cc155 (PR #38).

gen_configs.py.basis: recorded: staged to both hosts at launch; unchanged from this commit through the branch merge

run_experiments.py.basis: recorded: staged to both hosts at launch; unchanged from this commit through the branch merge

merge_experiments.py.basis: recorded: the revision that produced the merged CSVs locally on 2026-07-27

aurus_campaign.py.basis: recorded: the post-fix revision whose recovery pass wrote the final aurus_results CSVs (the initial pass ran f45ad18d - see caveats). Both hosts' on-disk copies still hash to this blob (checked 2026-07-31).

aurus_validate.py.basis: recorded: produced the aurus_validation CSVs on both hosts. Both hosts' on-disk copies still hash to this blob (checked 2026-07-31).
